title: What will any host or reporter say during ABC World News Tonight originally scheduled for October 19, 2026? Jalen Hurts
rules:
If 
 any host or reporter says Jalen Hurts as part of ABC World News Tonight originally scheduled for October 19, 2026
, then the market resolves to Yes.
rules_secondary:
Video of the ABC World News Tonight originally scheduled for October 19, 2026 will be primarily used to resolve the market; if a consensus by Kalshi employees cannot be reached using video, internal & external (official) transcripts of the ABC World News Tonight originally scheduled for October 19, 2026 will be used.

Payout Criterion: 
The exact phrase/word, or a plural or possessive form of the phrase/word, must be used. Grammatical/tense inflections are otherwise not included. 
Plural nouns occurring within proper nouns and noun phrases (e.g. names, titles, etc) are included.
For the purpose of this market, the live broadcast or stream will be used to resolve this event. 
Additional content not included in the original broadcast or stream will not count. 
Promotional content aired during the event will count, but advertisements will not. 
For the purpose of this market, the entirety of content within the original broadcast will be used for resolution.
Please see full rules for more details.

Postponement:
If the event is postponed, and such a postponement is announced by the end of the following calendar day to be rescheduled to a time within 14 calendar days, the markets shall remain open.

blind.reasoning: On October 19, 2026 itself, the Eagles announced that Jalen Hurts has DVT and blood clots in both lungs and will likely miss the season. That made it a major health and sports story, and ABC News' medical correspondents (Narula, Sutton) were already covering it. World News Tonight regularly covers star athletes' serious health scares, so a mention by name that evening is likely. The main risks are other heavy news pushing it out, or the story airing without his full name.
blind.falsifier: The October 19 broadcast airs without a Hurts segment, or covers it without anyone saying 'Jalen Hurts', for example because of breaking news like the France riots or another major domestic story.

final.reasoning: The low price suggests skepticism that World News Tonight covers NFL injuries, so I shaded down from 0.81. A same-day, season-ending pulmonary embolism diagnosis for a star QB, which ABC's medical team was already covering, still makes a named mention more likely than 36%.
